title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: GAR — parental crime can descend to unborn / nephews
pass_a_gloss: GAR's last: it is false to suppose parents' crime is never imputed to the yet-unborn or to grandsons. Many contrary examples stand ready—infamy, loss of honors, and exile often descend even on traitors' grandsons—and Scripture's examples will make that plain later.
pass_b_english: GAR. Finally, he assumes something false who supposes that parents' crime is never imputed to those yet to be born, or to grandsons: seeing that examples to the contrary are ready in plenty. For infamy, and deprivation of honors, and exile not infrequently descend even upon the grandsons of traitors. Which Scripture's examples will afterward also make plain.
source_text: GAR. Denique falsum assumit, qui supponit parentum crimen nunquam nascituris, aut nepotibus imputari: cum exempla in contrarium suppetant bene multa: Infamia enim, & honorum privatio, & exilium etiam in nepotes perduellium non infrequentur descendunt. Quod & Scripturae exempla postea manifestum facient.
